question: What term describes the non-medical conditions where people live and work that shape health outcomes?
explanation: Social determinants refer to the broad environmental and living conditions that influence health status. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h1)

question: Why must Nigerian nurses understand social determinants when dealing with reproductive health?

options.A: They replace the need for physical examinations
options.B: They dictate the exact surgical technique used
options.C: They explain why patients seek unsafe procedures

explanation: Recognizing social drivers helps nurses understand the complex pressures forcing individuals into risky abortion methods. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h1)

question: Financial barriers in resource-poor settings most often drive vulnerable patients to use what kind of services?
explanation: Lack of money forces patients to seek out cheap, unqualified practitioners who offer hazardous procedures. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h2)

question: A patient presents with severe sepsis after taking a cheap local concoction to end a pregnancy. What underlying factor is most likely at play?

options.A: Complete ignorance of basic human anatomy
options.B: A personal preference for traditional herbal medicine
options.C: An allergic reaction to standard hospital antibiotics
options.D: Severe financial constraints limiting access to safe care

explanation: Poverty often leaves individuals with no financial choice other than dangerous, low-cost alternatives. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h2)

question: What is the primary reason patients hide abortion complications from healthcare providers?

options.A: Preference for managing symptoms at home
options.B: Lack of available transport to the hospital
options.C: High cost of basic nursing consultation
options.D: Intense social stigma and fear of judgment

explanation: Fear of moral condemnation and community shame frequently stops people from admitting to induced abortions. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h3)

question: How do strict religious and cultural beliefs impact maternal morbidity rates in Nigeria?

options.A: They eliminate the need for emergency surgical interventions
options.B: They improve adherence to strict antenatal clinic guidelines
options.C: They guarantee financial support from community leaders
options.D: They delay timely treatment due to secrecy and shame

explanation: When communities heavily stigmatize abortion, patients wait until complications become life-threatening before seeking help. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h3)

question: A low level of formal education is most directly linked to which of the following?

options.A: Greater financial stability in urban centers
options.B: Increased access to safe surgical specialists
options.D: Higher reliance on dangerous contraceptive myths

explanation: Limited education restricts access to factual health knowledge, leaving people vulnerable to widespread myths. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h4)

question: Why does poor health literacy worsen the outcomes of unwanted pregnancies?

options.A: It prevents individuals from identifying safe medical options
options.B: It guarantees free treatment in government clinics
options.C: It automatically makes federal laws much stricter
options.D: It reduces the physical pain of botched procedures

explanation: Without adequate health literacy, patients cannot separate safe healthcare practices from dangerous quackery. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h4)

question: Under Nigerian law, when is an abortion generally permitted?

options.A: Only when necessary to save the pregnant person's life
options.B: In cases of severe financial hardship or poverty
options.C: During the first trimester for any medical reason
options.D: Whenever the individual requests it in writing

explanation: The Penal and Criminal Codes in Nigeria strictly limit legal termination to saving the life of the mother. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h5)

question: What is a major unintended consequence of restrictive abortion laws in clinical practice?

options.A: The cost of safe hospital procedures drops significantly
options.B: All unwanted pregnancies are successfully prevented
options.C: Qualified providers refuse care out of fear of arrest
options.D: Traditional herbal remedies become scientifically validated

explanation: Strict legal penalties often frighten legitimate medical professionals away from performing safe terminations or providing open care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h5)

question: Unequal gender power dynamics in relationships most often result in what for women?

options.A: Total control over household financial budgets
options.B: Reduced autonomy over personal reproductive decisions
options.C: Guaranteed financial support from male partners
options.D: Immediate access to quality maternal healthcare

explanation: Male-dominated household structures often strip women of their right to make independent choices about contraception and pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h6)

question: A young female student is abandoned by her partner after a pregnancy test is positive. What immediate risk is she most vulnerable to?

options.A: Receiving free comprehensive care at a tertiary hospital
options.B: Gaining immediate support from traditional rulers
options.C: Attempting a secret, unsafe abortion due to isolation
options.D: Experiencing rapid resolution of the unwanted pregnancy

explanation: Lack of partner support combined with social shame drives vulnerable persons to seek out dangerous, clandestine solutions. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h6)

question: Which setting in Nigeria typically suffers from a severe shortage of skilled reproductive health personnel?
explanation: Rural areas consistently lack basic medical infrastructure and qualified healthcare professionals compared to cities. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h7)

question: Why do maternal mortality rates from unsafe abortions tend to be higher in remote villages than in cities?

options.A: Rural doctors perform more advanced surgical procedures
options.B: Village residents have better health insurance coverage
options.C: Rural patients lack access to emergency medical facilities
options.D: Traditional herbs are completely non-toxic and effective

explanation: Geographical isolation prevents rural patients from reaching professional care in time when post-abortion complications arise. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h7)

question: What is the nurse's primary legal and ethical duty when treating a patient with abortion complications?

options.A: To lecture the patient on moral standards
options.B: To refuse treatment based on personal beliefs
options.C: To report the patient to local law enforcement
options.D: To provide immediate life-saving medical care

explanation: Professional ethics demand that preserving human life and managing acute medical emergencies always come before moral judgment. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h8)

question: How does displaying a judgmental attitude affect a patient suffering from a botched abortion?

options.A: It successfully convinces the patient to change their lifestyle
options.B: It discourages honest disclosure and delays critical treatment
options.C: It improves overall compliance with hospital discharge rules
options.D: It speeds up the surgical recovery process in the ward

explanation: Hostility from healthcare workers makes patients hide vital medical history, worsening their clinical outcomes. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h8)
